title: Working with product: discovery, trade-offs and a roadmap with two authors

videos.script: Most engineering teams meet a product idea for the first time as a specification. {{spec}} By then the expensive questions have been answered without them. Can it be built? On this system? By these people? This lesson puts engineers back at the start, with Marty Cagan's four risks. Value, usability, feasibility and viability. {{risks}} Then it deals with the argument that fills every planning meeting. A feature and a piece of debt are compared one at a time, and the debt loses, every time. Coreto settles it once a year instead, with a share of capacity agreed in advance. {{split}} Last, the roadmap. Coreto used to have two, one from product and one from engineering, and both counted on the same people. Now it has one, with two authors. Júlia writes the product themes. Davi writes the engineering themes. And the arrows between them explain the order. {{roadmap}} By the end you can bring engineering into a product conversation early, and keep it there when the quarter gets tight. {{end}}
